hints.content:
First, we see that the relationship *is* proportional.  The point $(\pink0,\blue0)$ is in the table, and for an increase of $1.3$ in $x$, there is an increase of $1$ in $y$.  Let’s find the unit rate of change of $y$ with respect to $x$: what is the $y$-value corresponding to $x=\pink1?$

$\begin{align}\dfrac{\blue1}{\pink{1.3}}&=\dfrac{\blue1}{\pink{\dfrac{13}{10}}}\\ &\\&\\&\\
&=\blue1\cdot\pink{\dfrac{10}{13}}\\&\\&=\dfrac{10}{13}\end{align}$ 

 This is the unit rate of change of $y$ with respect to $x$, and the point $\left(\pink1,\blue{\dfrac{10}{13}}\right)$ lies on the line.  However, to graph the line representing the relationship, it will be helpful to find another point on the line.

The graph goes through $(\pink0,\blue0)$.   Because the unit rate is $\dfrac{10}{13}$ , a change of $\pink{13}$ units in $x$ results in an increase of $\dfrac{10}{13}(\pink{13})=\blue{10}$ units in $y$.  So the point $(\pink{13},\blue{{10}})$  lies on the graph.    Now we can draw the line connecting these two points.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: An XY coordinate plane divided into four quadrants. The horizontal x axis runs left to right from negative 14 to 14 in intervals of 1. The vertical y axis runs up and down from negative 14 to 14 in intervals of 1. The graph passes through the points (negative 13, negative 10), (0, 0), and (13, 10). Closed points are plotted at (0, 0) and (13, 10).

hints.content:
Since the graph goes through $(\pink0,\blue0)$ and $(\pink{13},\blue{10})$, 
 the slope is

$\dfrac{\left(\blue{10}-\blue0\right)}{(\pink{13}-\pink0)}=\dfrac{10}{13}$ , the same as the unit rate of change.
